seo_description: Free, open-source macOS clipboard manager. A docked sidebar sorts history into text, links, images, colors and files, with text transforms. Opens with ⌥⌘V.
hero_sub: A docked sidebar that sorts everything you copy into text, links, images, colors and files. Press ⌥⌘V to open it, then hit Return to paste back into the app you were using.
features_sub: Everything below is in the app today and runs locally on your Mac.

features.title: Automatic type sorting
features.desc: Each copy is classified as text, rich text, link, image, color or file list. Filter chips and search narrow the list quickly.

features.title: Docked right-edge sidebar
features.desc: A 340 pt panel opens from the right edge by hotkey, from the menu bar, or optionally by pushing the pointer against the screen edge.

features.title: Built-in text transforms
features.desc: Right-click an item to apply UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, Trim Whitespace, Remove Line Breaks, Sort Lines or Wrap in Quotes.

features.title: Keyboard-first pasting
features.desc: Use the arrow keys to move, Return to paste, Shift+Return for plain text, Command-P to pin and Command-Delete to remove.

features.title: Privacy-minded capture
features.desc: Items flagged as concealed or transient are skipped, and 1Password and Bitwarden are ignored by default. You can add more ignored apps.

features.title: Pinning and retention
features.desc: Keep 50 to 500 items and expire them after 1 to 365 days, or never. Pinned items are never expired or cleared.

permissions_step: Optionally grant Accessibility in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility so ClipTypeSidebar can paste directly into the previous app; without it, items are copied and you press Command-V yourself.

faq.q: Is ClipTypeSidebar free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is free and released under the MIT license, with the full source on GitHub. There are no accounts, subscriptions or paid tiers; if it saves you time, you can optionally support development through Ko-fi.

Only Accessibility, and only if you want it to paste directly into the app you were using, since it sends a synthetic Command-V. It asks on demand with an explanation first. Without it, the item is copied and you paste manually. Launch at login is also optional.

faq.q: Where is my clipboard data stored?
faq.a: Only on your Mac. History is a JSON file in ~/Library/Application Support/ClipTypeSidebar, with copied images saved as PNG files beside it. The code contains no networking, so nothing is uploaded.

Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, which this free project does not have. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode and XcodeGen.
